transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I’m just... I'm exhausted. And it's in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. Just getting through a normal workday and then managing dinner at home—it all just feels so much heavier than it should right now.
Over this period when you've been feeling exhausted, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling sad, empty, or down—or have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just... I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. So, yes, feeling down is definitely there right along with the exhaustion.

Besides the exhaustion and heavy mood you've described, have you been experiencing worry or anxiety—maybe racing thoughts, restlessness, or a sense of dread—even on days when things are going relatively okay?

No, not really. I mean... I don't think I've been feeling anxious or worried. It's not like my thoughts are racing at all. Honestly, if anything, my mind just feels kind of slow and blank lately. I don't have a sense of dread or restlessness, it's really just... just the lack of energy and feeling down.
How long have you been feeling this way—this exhaustion and heavy mood? Can you give me a sense of when it started?

I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. It was actually a pretty noticeable shift... before this started, I was feeling unusually energized and really driven at work. But then it just swung into this persistently low feeling, and I've been stuck in this heavy exhaustion for the last four weeks or so.

You mentioned that before this month-long period, you were feeling unusually energized and driven at work. During that time, did you notice anything else different about yourself—like feeling unusually happy or confident, needing less sleep than normal, or feeling like your thoughts were moving faster than usual?

Yeah, the sleep was definitely the biggest difference. During that stretch, I was sleeping... maybe four hours a night? But I wasn't tired at all. I'd just wake up and feel completely ready to go. I'd be up early, ready to send out work emails, sketch out event ideas, or even reorganize my whole kitchen before anyone else was even awake. So, yes, I definitely needed a lot less sleep than normal.

During that time when you were sleeping only four hours and felt so energized and driven—how was your actual mood then? Were you feeling unusually happy, excited, or on top of the world? Or was it more just that you had the energy and drive to do things?

Well, my mood was definitely... different. I'd say I had this unusually charged, upbeat mood. I felt like my ideas were just brilliant. But it wasn't just all happy and excited. I noticed that I would get irritated really fast if my husband questioned any of my plans. So, I guess it was a mix of feeling great one minute, and then getting pretty annoyed the next if someone tried to slow me down.
